item.title: as long as you promise not to make me do anything about the result
item.description:
by keya singh and ioanna loup
the body provides us a sensual experience of itself, others and the world. in return, it demands care and concern – often requiring professional intervention. with its roots in mark fisher’s texts about “the eerie”, this film explores such interventions with a focus on ophthalmology and one patient’s inner voice during those interventions. the eerie is the failure of presence and the failure of absence. and our eyes contribute to these failures.

item.title: Insomnia Festival 2021
item.description: I was invited to create visuals for 3 sets back-to-back for Insomnia Festival’s kick-off event at Storgata Camping (Tromsø, Norway). The first two sets lasted about 1 hour each while the last one was 3 hours long. So far the longest set I have made, this was a great opportunity to see how far I can go with maintaining a sense of live-ness and control even when the material feels like it has already been exhausted.

item.title: #jpeg2dicom
item.description:
Ongoing experiments using a CT scan reader to compress video frames into objects that can be manipulated in 3D. This curiosity was born while attending an online workshop, “Creative and Artistic Use of Medical Imagery” led by Haraldur Karlsson and organised by Vašulka Kitchen Brno in April-May 2020.

Since the workshop, I have been testing material in terms of footage (filmed, found, images in motion) and colours. My aim for the future is to convert these objects into 3D files that can be used in 3D and VR environments.
